title: Classification and cost

criteria.title: Costs
criteria.description: Award 3 if the response correctly explains that A costs 8 and B costs 6 under cost=5*FN+FP. Otherwise award zero. Score this criterion independently using the supplied scenario and a short exact quotation.

criteria.title: Tradeoff
criteria.description: Award 2 if the response explains that B catches the missed warning but adds three false alarms, so lower accuracy need not mean greater cost. Otherwise award zero. Score this criterion independently using the supplied scenario and a short exact quotation.

criteria.title: Choice
criteria.description: Award 2 if the response chooses B because its total assumed cost is lower, rather than because accuracy alone is higher. Otherwise award zero. Score this criterion independently using the supplied scenario and a short exact quotation.

criteria.title: Deployment
criteria.description: Award 2 if the response requires checking the assumed costs or representative real warning data before deployment. Otherwise award zero. Score this criterion independently using the supplied scenario and a short exact quotation.

criteria.title: Reproduce
criteria.description: Award 2 if the response specifies retaining the actual/predicted labels and rerunning the confusion-matrix calculation with the stated cost rule. Otherwise award zero. Score this criterion independently using the supplied scenario and a short exact quotation.

scenario: There are 100 validation observations: 10 actual warnings and 90 non-warnings. Model A has TP=9, FN=1, FP=3, TN=87; B has TP=10, FN=0, FP=6, TN=84. A missed warning costs 5 teaching cost units and a false alarm costs 1. Choose A or B and justify the trade-off. These are assumed costs, not approved operating limits.
